merged_candidates.role: SVP and Chief Medical Information Officer
merged_candidates.anchorage_tie: DISPUTED. Palis is based in Renton, WA. Anchorage tie is bowl-impact only: Providence Alaska Medical Center is one of 51 hospitals in the Providence system, but Palis's role is system-wide. Not bowl-resident or Anchorage-domiciled. Bowl-impact tiebreaker: Providence Alaska Medical Center is a major Anchorage healthcare institution and any system-wide AI consolidation decision directly affects clinical AI deployment there.

decision.what_happened: On May 27, 2026, Providence announced an 'Epic-first' AI consolidation strategy, committing to route all clinical AI through Epic's integrated AI tools and discontinuing standalone AI products across the 51-hospital system. Palis led and publicly announced this decision.
decision.binary_owned: Palis, as SVP and CMIO, chose to consolidate all clinical AI through Epic's platform, retiring standalone AI products, committing the entire 51-hospital system including Providence Alaska Medical Center to a single integrated AI architecture.
decision.ak_consequence: Healthcare AI sector; all AI clinical tools at Providence Alaska Medical Center (Anchorage's largest hospital) consolidated through Epic. Affects clinical decision support, predictive analytics, and AI-assisted diagnostics for Alaska patients.

merged_candidates.validator_flag: Gate 1 RISK: Palis is Renton WA-based. Anchorage tie is bowl-impact only, not bowl-residency. Validator must determine if bowl-impact satisfies Anchorage-tie gate.

merged_candidates.anchorage_tie: GCI is headquartered in Anchorage; Goldie is Anchorage-based as CTO of Alaska's largest telecom.

decision.ak_consequence: Rural broadband expansion; improved connectivity for rural Alaska communities.

decision.what_happened: McCormick sponsored AR 2026-129 on approximately May 12, 2026, calling for review of JBER fence proposal. The resolution asks JBER to consider 'alternative means for securing the base' which the environmental assessment lists as including motion sensors and surveillance cameras.
decision.binary_owned: McCormick introduced a resolution pushing JBER to consider surveillance technology alternatives to a physical fence.
decision.ak_consequence: Security infrastructure; potential delay of JBER fence construction; opens discussion of surveillance tech alternatives.

subject_quotes.verbatim: I'm not saying they can't build the fence. I just want to make sure that we know what the impact is going to be and that they're open to alternative means for securing the base.

merged_candidates.validator_flag: Gate 3 LIKELY FAIL (SECOND TIME): AR 2026-129 concerns NEPA review of a physical fence. It does not adopt, fund, block, or mandate any AI or surveillance technology — it asks for impact review and consideration of alternatives. Previously failed Gate 3 in 2026-05-20 validator run. The 'alternative means' language references surveillance tech in the environmental assessment but McCormick's resolution does not choose, fund, or mandate it.
